tool.name: Select informative features
tool.command:
mkdir pycytominer_output &&
## Convert the input to CSV for pycytominer #if $profiles.ext in ["tsv", "tabular"] python '$__tool_directory__/format_converter_csvtsv.py' -i '$profiles' -o 'profiles.csv' -c tsv2csv && #else cp '$profiles' 'profiles.csv' && #end if
pycytominer feature_select
--profiles 'profiles.csv' --output_file './pycytominer_output/output.csv' --output_type 'csv' --operation "${', '.join($operation)}" &&
## Convert the result back to TSV for the Galaxy dataset python '$__tool_directory__/format_converter_csvtsv.py' -i 'pycytominer_output/output.csv' -o '$output' -c csv2tsv

param.name: profiles
param.label: Input cell-profiling table
param.help: Table with features extracted from biological images, normally after normalization

param.name: operation
param.label: Select operations
param.help: List of operation to apply to the cell-profiling table

tool.help:
**What it does**
**Pycytominer Feature Select** removes uninformative features. Multiple operations can be applied in one call by passing a comma-delimited list.
- **Variance Threshold**, drop near-constant features
- **Correlation Threshold**, drop one of each highly correlated pair
- **Blocklist**, drop features known to be unreliable across assays
- **Drop NA Columns**, drop columns with too many missing values
- **Noise Removal**, remove features with low signal-to-noise ratio
Documentation: https://pycytominer.readthedocs.io/en/stable/index.html
